family.tagline: Radio logbooks, quilting patterns and a library of their own.
family.story: Winston is a retired machinist who has kept radio logbooks for fifty years. Adaeze is a retired librarian who quilts and keeps a reading list. Their grandson Kelechi visits on weekends, and one Companion Core sits on a shelf in the living room.

companion.name: Percy
companion.job: Opens Kiwix in its own browser and pulls up the manual Winston names.
companion.limits: Pulls up a page. Winston reads it.

companion.name: Opal
companion.job: Finds the book or pattern Adaeze asks about, from what she put in Companion Memory.
companion.limits: Finds and reports. Adaeze opens and decides.

popup.title: A parcel, carried by a grandson
popup.body: The parcel arrives on a Friday, as Kelechi does. He carries it through the vestibule and entry hall to the living room. Winston rolls ahead on his scooter.

popup.title: Everything in the parcel
popup.body: Winston lifts out the Companion Core, a power cable and a recovery USB drive. Adaeze reads the quick-start guide. The Core covers about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Winston plugs in the cable. Adaeze presses the button, and the Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: Winston joins the Core's own Wi-Fi network from his phone. Then he picks the home network.

popup.title: Choose the first agents
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Adaeze picks Hermes and Winston picks OpenClaw. They add Companion Memory (beta), Kiwix and Koodo Reader, then settle into their chairs.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Opal says good evening
popup.body: Adaeze sends the first message to Opal, the agent she named. Opal answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: adaeze
say.text: Good evening, Adaeze. I am Opal. What shall we find first?

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off

popup.title: Where the chapter stopped
popup.body: Winston settles into the bay window loveseat. Audiobookshelf starts his book right where he stopped, from the library on the Core.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Old photographs by the fire
popup.body: Beside the fireplace, Adaeze and Kelechi look through old family pictures in Immich. The whole library sits on the Core.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: Lamps that come on at dusk
popup.body: At dusk, the lamps in the fireside nook come on by themselves, on a Home Assistant schedule. It runs on the Core over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner

popup.title: Recipe cards, typed at last
popup.body: At the breakfast bar, Adaeze types her mother's recipe cards into KitchenOwl, a few each evening. The recipe book lives on the Core.

beats.capability: lists, boards and calendars for tasks, with reminders and recurring jobs

popup.title: The weekend list has reminders
popup.body: Winston keeps the weekend jobs in Vikunja, with a reminder for each. The gutters come first, and the list lives on the Core.

beats.capability: archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at

popup.title: The oven's papers, filed
popup.body: Winston files the new oven's receipt and papers in Papra. They wait there, on the Core, until a question comes up.

beats.capability: a daily journal in plain Markdown files

popup.title: A new line in the log
popup.body: At the dining table, Winston types the day's radio contacts into Logseq. One page a day, as plain files on the Core.

beats.capability: read Wikipedia and other reference sites

popup.title: Percy finds the article
popup.body: Winston asks Percy for the article on dipole antennas. Percy opens Kiwix in its own browser and pulls it up. Winston reads it, pencil in hand.

say.speaker: winston
say.text: Here is the article. Please read it.

beats.capability: track the films, shows, books and games you have watched, read and played

popup.title: The reading list, kept up
popup.body: Adaeze keeps her reading list in Yamtrack: the books she has finished and the ones still waiting. It began on paper, in her library days.

beats.capability: run a quiz night for a small group

popup.title: Kelechi hosts the quiz
popup.body: On Saturday night, Kelechi hosts a quiz in Razzia at the dining table. Adaeze keeps score, and Winston argues the radio questions.

beats.capability: read ebooks in your browser, with notes and highlights

popup.title: A novel and a highlighted line
popup.body: At the desk in the guest room, Kelechi reads a novel in Koodo Reader. He highlights a line to show his grandmother. The library lives on the Core.

beats.capability: keeps your digital life on your own disk; imports are opt-in

popup.title: Opal finds the quilt photo
popup.body: Adaeze asks Opal which pattern she used for the blue quilt. Opal finds the photo Adaeze chose to put in Companion Memory. Adaeze opens it herself.

say.speaker: adaeze
say.text: I found the photo. Please open it to check.

beats.capability: draw logos, diagrams and line art as vector graphics, in your browser

popup.title: A quilt block, drawn first
popup.body: Adaeze draws a new quilt block in Inkscape, in her browser. It is line art now and fabric next week.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Sunday music on the deck
popup.body: On Sunday, Kelechi plays his favorite albums from Navidrome on the deck. The collection streams from the Core to his phone.

beats.capability: plan, map and share hiking and biking routes from GPX files

popup.title: A walk planned from the deck
popup.body: Winston and Kelechi load a GPX route into Wanderer and plan the afternoon's walk from the deck. The route lives on the Core.

popup.title: One Core, one shelf
popup.body: The Bellamy-Nwosu household keeps its logbooks, its reading list and its weekends on one Core in the living room.

closing.body: Your logbook, your reading list and your quilting patterns can live on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: FTUE follows the owner's hotspot flow (STORY-BIBLE section 7); owner sign-off against the fact sheet is still open.
No TV in this home: the media beat is Audiobookshelf at the couch (the bay window loveseat). The words TV and screen are not used.
Winston rides a mobility scooter (cast leaves it open which spouse). Mentioned once, as a fact, in ftue-delivery.
dining-reference: Kiwix needs its content files downloaded once; the text does not say offline. Percy opens a local app, not a website.
guest-opal is the Finder persona: Hermes drafts and reports, Adaeze opens and decides. Companion Memory is opt-in. Invented place and street: check Quarry Wick and Sparrow Mill Road against a map.
